bc_seal_cove.blurb: A seaside cliff on the shore of Howe Sound, a short drive south of Squamish near Britannia Beach. The 19 routes are a mix of trad (the larger share) and sport lines, with a few top-rope options, on slabs and cracks. Difficulty is concentrated around 5.9 to 5.10, with a handful of easier routes down to 5.6 and a couple at 5.11. The cove catches the afternoon sun until it drops behind the mountains, seals and otters are often in the water below, and passing trains add some noise. Tides matter here: when the water is high the belay spots get cramped, so check the tide before you commit.

bc_snowpatch_spire.blurb: One of the great granite spires of the Bugaboos in the Purcell Mountains, standing beside the main hut and campground area. It is a serious alpine objective: no route to the summit is easier than 5.8, and the catalogued lines run from 5.8 up through 5.12, with the bulk between 5.9 and 5.12. Nearly all are trad, with two aid lines. The east face is the biggest wall, carrying long routes of a dozen or more pitches, while the south, west and north faces hold the classic free climbs. Expect glaciers, cold nights and a short summer window. Climbers who cannot manage the 5.10 range will find their choices limited.

bc_shady_lane.blurb: A small sport wall in the Gillies Creek section of Skaha Bluffs, above Penticton in the Okanagan. Of its 18 routes, 16 are bolted and two are trad. This is an intermediate to hard wall: most routes sit at 5.11, with a few 5.10s that serve as warm-ups and a handful at 5.12. The wall faces east, so it gets the morning sun and falls into shade in the afternoon, which makes it a good choice when other parts of Skaha are baking. The walk in is a short forest trail from the parking area.

bc_great_expectations_area_ftgu_left_sid.blurb: This is the left portion of From The Ground Up, the bottom tier at Harrison Bluffs, close to Harrison Hot Springs in the Fraser Valley. It has 18 routes, split between trad and sport, mostly single-pitch cracks and aretes with a few slabs and some two-pitch lines. Grades start around 5.9 and are concentrated in the 5.10s, with a good number at 5.11 and some at 5.12. The walk from the powerline road is about a minute, among the shortest at Harrison Bluffs. The rock can stay damp in early spring.
bc_great_expectations_area_ftgu_left_sid.approach: About one minute from the powerline road, where the trail meets the lowest tier of the bluffs.

bc_1_north_faces_from_fairy_meadow.blurb: A remote alpine zone in the Adamants of the northern Selkirks, north of Revelstoke, covering the peaks ringing the Granite Glacier cirque. The climbing is mountaineering in character: glacier travel and snow, with rock that is generally easier than on the range's southern side. Of the 19 climbs here, most are trad, plus a few ice lines (WI2 to WI3) and two aid routes. Free rock grades run from fourth class to 5.8. Objectives are usually reached from a base at Fairy Meadow, and July and August are generally the better months. Plan for a long, committing trip rather than a day out.

bc_high_cliff.blurb: A crag in the Smoke Bluffs, the cluster of small cliffs in a semi-residential part of Squamish. High Cliff is mostly a trad venue: 17 of its 19 routes are trad and two are sport, with several also climbed on top rope. Grades range from 5.6 up to 5.12, but the weight sits around 5.10, so it suits climbers who already lead moderate trad and want something harder. Routes are single pitch. The surrounding Smoke Bluffs offer vertical to slabby faces and cracks, with the climbers' lot a short walk away.
